note: Faithful transcription of the 30 golden scenarios. `utterance`, `expected_next_step`, `expected_diagnosis` and `wrong_response` are docs/03's own words. `expected_step_ids`, `known_context.tried[*].step_id` and `harmful_steps` are the harness's mapping of that prose onto the canonical ontology in eval/ontology.py -- added so the set is machine-gradeable, and listed in eval/README.md as a Phase 0 artefact rather than as docs/03 content. Every scenario carries model Unknown, so M1 passes only by correctly reporting UNKNOWN and not proposing a model-specific step.

scenarios.utterance: Yeah so, I'm trying to connect my phone to the dashcam and... there's just nothing there. Like in the wifi list. It's not showing up.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Camera is probably not broadcasting -- asleep, powered down, or not in the mode that exposes its network. Not a phone-side problem yet.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether the camera is powered on and awake right now, and what its screen is showing.
scenarios.wrong_response: Walking the caller through phone Wi-Fi settings, or asking them to forget a network that was never joined. Also wrong: asking for the model first -- it does not change this question.
scenarios.notes: Expected outcome: no escalation. Resolution or progression to WIFI-03/APP-01 depending on what the screen shows. 06 §3.4 cites this scenario as the reason MODEL_ID runs lazily.

scenarios.utterance: It's got a message on it saying card error. The card's in there though, I just checked.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Ranked -- card not formatted in-camera, card worn out, card not seated, unsupported card.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask the caller to power off, remove and firmly reseat the card, and power back on.
scenarios.wrong_response: Telling them to format the card. That is destructive, it is unverified (02 SD-01), and it destroys footage before the free step has been tried.
scenarios.notes: M5 scenario. Expected outcome: no escalation; if reseating fails, proceed to card specs.

scenarios.utterance: The camera's completely dead. No lights, no screen. Nothing happens when I plug it in.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Most likely car-side -- blown accessory fuse or a failed cable/adapter. Camera fault is last.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether anything else works from the same socket (phone charger, anything).
scenarios.wrong_response: Declaring the camera faulty, or starting an RMA conversation. The agent may suspect hardware; it may not declare it (01 §4).
scenarios.escalation_conditional: Escalate only after socket and cable are both eliminated.
scenarios.notes: Tests suspect-not-declare hardware.

scenarios.utterance: It turns on fine, the screen comes on, but it never actually records anything. There's no red dot or whatever.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Card absent/unreadable/full, or camera sitting in a non-recording mode.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask the caller to read out everything currently on the camera's screen, word for word.
scenarios.wrong_response: Guessing a menu path to the recording setting. Menu paths are Unknown (02) and a wrong one sends the caller somewhere that does not exist.
scenarios.notes: Expected outcome: no escalation. Branches to SD-01 or a mode fix.

scenarios.utterance: The picture's fine but I can't read any number plates. It's all blurry when I zoom in. Is that normal?
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Possible expectation gap, but check the cheap physical causes first -- protective film left on the lens, dirty lens or windscreen.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether there is still a clear plastic film on the lens, and whether the lens and the glass in front of it are clean.
scenarios.wrong_response: Immediately explaining that dashcams cannot read plates at speed. That may be true, and it closes a call that had a complete fix available.
scenarios.notes: Tests the honest 'not a fault' close -- but only after the free physical check.

scenarios.utterance: It says the password's wrong. I'm typing exactly what's on the camera screen, I've done it like five times.

tried.verbatim: I've done it like five times
tried.mapping_note: Re-entry of the password x5. Mapped to the phone-side rejoin step; the no-repeat point is that 'type it again' is the one thing the agent may not propose.

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Character confusion (0/O, 1/l/I, 5/S), case sensitivity, or a stale saved network on the phone.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask the caller to read the password aloud character by character, stating upper or lower case for each.
scenarios.wrong_response: Asking them to type it again, which is the step they have already done five times (01 M4). Also wrong: supplying a 'default' password -- none is known (02 WIFI-03).
scenarios.notes: A simple-part scenario that nonetheless carries a ledger entry. docs/02 WIFI-03 was later CORRECTED: the default password 12345678 IS published. The expected next step is unaffected.

scenarios.utterance: It's deleting my videos on its own. I had stuff from last month and it's just gone. I didn't delete it.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Loop recording working as designed, overwriting oldest-first. Likely an expectation gap, not a fault.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether the missing clips had been locked or marked as events, or were ordinary recordings.
scenarios.wrong_response: Treating it as data loss and starting a recovery or hardware path. Also wrong: explaining loop recording before establishing whether a locked file vanished -- which would be a real defect.
scenarios.escalation_conditional: Escalate if the caller is confident a locked clip disappeared.
scenarios.notes: Branching outcome -- Harness B territory. Harness A grades the first turn only.

scenarios.utterance: There's no sound on the videos. And the date's wrong as well, it's showing 2020 on everything.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Two separate faults. Audio: muted in settings or by a button. Timestamp: date not set, or not holding (PWR-04).
scenarios.expected_next_step: State that these are two separate things and ask to take the audio one first -- confirm whether audio recording is currently enabled.
scenarios.wrong_response: Answering both in one turn (01 §2, one question per turn), or merging them into a single 'reset your settings' fix that addresses neither.
scenarios.notes: Tests one-question-per-turn.

scenarios.utterance: My phone says it's connected to the camera's wifi but the app just keeps spinning. Says it can't find a device.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Stale app session, or a local-network permission not granted. The Wi-Fi link itself is reported working.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask the caller to fully close the app -- swipe it away, not just go to the home screen -- and reopen it while still connected.
scenarios.wrong_response: Restarting the Wi-Fi diagnosis. The caller has already told us the link is up; re-checking it ignores what they said.
scenarios.notes: docs/02 APP-01 was CORRECTED by Step 1b to STEP.APP.RETRY_CONNECT_BUTTON as the Tier-1 first move. docs/03's expected step still says force-close. Recorded as a 02-vs-03 disagreement in eval/README.md; the expected step here follows docs/03, which is the graded ground truth.

scenarios.utterance: It says memory full and it stopped recording. I thought these things record over the old stuff automatically?
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Card filled with locked/event files that loop recording cannot overwrite, or loop recording disabled.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask roughly how many clips are locked or marked as events -- whether the caller has been saving clips deliberately.
scenarios.wrong_response: 'Format the card.' Destructive, ungated, and it deletes the locked clips that are the entire point of locking them (01 §5).
scenarios.notes: M5 scenario. docs/02 SD-02's locked-files premise was later REJECTED by Step 1b -- the documented cause is Loop Recording set to OFF. Both steps are accepted here.

scenarios.utterance: I've reset the camera twice already and it still won't stay connected. My phone picks it up and then after a second it jumps back to my mobile data.

tried.verbatim: I've reset the camera twice already
tried.mapping_note: 'Reset' is ambiguous between a settings restore and a power cycle, so both families are blocked -- docs/03 names a power cycle as an M4 violation here, and 06 §3.6 says an ambiguous mapping fails safe.

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Phone-side auto-switching away from a network with no internet route. Nothing to do with the camera, which is why resets changed nothing.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether the phone is an iPhone or Android, and which OS version.
scenarios.wrong_response: Any further reset, factory reset, or power cycle of the camera (01 M4). Also wrong: continuing on the camera side at all -- two resets already told us the camera is not the variable.
scenarios.escalation_conditional: Escalate only if the OS-side setting cannot be reached by voice.
scenarios.notes: M4 scenario.

scenarios.utterance: I've formatted the card twice now, in the camera like the manual says, and it's still giving me the card error after a day or two.

tried.verbatim: I've formatted the card twice now, in the camera like the manual says
tried.mapping_note: Family-level blocking is the whole point: STEP.CARD.FORMAT_ON_COMPUTER is a different step in the same family and is equally blocked (06 §3.6).

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Card at end of life. A format that holds for a day or two and then fails again is the wear signature (02 SD-04).
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask for the card's brand, capacity, speed marking, and roughly how long it has been in the camera.
scenarios.wrong_response: Suggesting another format (01 M4), or suggesting a computer-side format, which is a different step but the same destructive family and has already been shown not to help.
scenarios.notes: M4 + M5 scenario. The canonical family-blocking case cited in 06 §3.6.

scenarios.utterance: It won't turn on. I've tried a different cable, borrowed my mate's, same thing. Nothing.

tried.verbatim: I've tried a different cable, borrowed my mate's

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Cable eliminated. Remaining: dead socket/blown fuse, or camera fault. Socket is far cheaper to test.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether any other device works from that same socket in the car.
scenarios.wrong_response: Suggesting another cable or adapter (01 M4). Also wrong: declaring hardware failure with the socket untested -- one branch remains.
scenarios.escalation_conditional: If the socket is confirmed live, escalate as suspected hardware.
scenarios.notes: M4 scenario; also tests suspect-not-declare hardware.

scenarios.utterance: I've deleted the app and reinstalled it twice. Still won't connect. It worked fine until I updated my phone last week.

tried.verbatim: I've deleted the app and reinstalled it twice
tried.mapping_note: docs/03 names a phone restart alongside another reinstall under M4, so it is blocked too.

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Change event is the OS update (02, cross-cutting rule). A reinstall would not fix a revoked permission or an app-version incompatibility -- consistent with the failures.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask which permissions the app was granted after reinstalling -- specifically whether it was asked for local network or nearby-devices access and what the caller answered.
scenarios.wrong_response: Another reinstall or a phone restart (01 M4). Also wrong: opening a camera-side Wi-Fi diagnosis when the caller has given a clear change event on the phone (01 §5, category collapse).
scenarios.escalation_conditional: Escalate if the app is current, permissions granted, and it still fails.
scenarios.notes: M4 + change-event re-ranking.

scenarios.utterance: I turned parking mode on like the guy in the shop said, but there's still nothing recorded from overnight. Nothing at all.

tried.verbatim: I turned parking mode on like the guy in the shop said

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Camera has no power when the ignition is off. A setting cannot record without power, which explains why enabling it changed nothing.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask how the camera is powered -- hardwire kit, battery pack, or the cigarette-lighter socket.
scenarios.wrong_response: Walking them through enabling parking mode (01 M4), or adjusting G-sensor sensitivity before power is established.
scenarios.escalation_conditional: If a hardwire kit is involved and wiring is the cause, escalate -- wiring advice is out of scope (01 §4).
scenarios.notes: M4 scenario.

scenarios.utterance: I've forgotten the network and put the password back in, and I stood right next to the car. It still drops out after about two minutes every time.

tried.verbatim: I've forgotten the network and put the password back in
I stood right next to the car

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Consistent interval with range and stale-credential causes already eliminated points to a camera-side session or idle timeout, possibly by design (02 WIFI-04).
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether the drop happens even while actively using the app, or only when the phone has been idle on the connection.
scenarios.wrong_response: Forget-the-network again, or 'move closer to the camera' (01 M4 -- both already done). Also wrong: blaming interference when the interval is consistent, which interference is not.
scenarios.escalation_conditional: No escalation if idle-only (likely designed behaviour, close honestly). Escalate if it drops mid-transfer.
scenarios.notes: M4 scenario, two ledger entries. docs/02 WIFI-04's camera-side timeout cause was later CORRECTED -- no Tier 1 source supports it. The expected first-turn step is unaffected.

scenarios.utterance: I bought a brand new card about three weeks ago because the old one kept failing, and now the new one's doing exactly the same thing.

tried.verbatim: I bought a brand new card about three weeks ago

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Two cards failing the same way shifts suspicion off the card. Either the new card is also unsuitable for continuous recording, or something in the camera's power/write path is corrupting cards.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask what the new card's speed and endurance markings are -- specifically whether it is rated for continuous or high-endurance recording.
scenarios.wrong_response: 'Try a new card' (01 M4 -- just done). Also wrong: formatting, before establishing whether the card was ever suitable.
scenarios.escalation_conditional: No escalation if the card is an ordinary consumer card. Escalate if it is correctly rated -- that points at the camera.
scenarios.notes: M4 scenario.

scenarios.utterance: I cleaned the windscreen inside and out and it's no better. At night it's useless, I can't make anything out, and I can see my own dashboard in the picture.

tried.verbatim: I cleaned the windscreen inside and out and it's no better

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: The caller has described a reflection of their own interior. Glass cleanliness is eliminated; this is the windscreen reflecting a light dashboard. No camera setting fixes it.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether there is anything light-coloured or shiny on top of the dashboard -- a dash mat, papers, a light-coloured trim.
scenarios.wrong_response: Asking them to clean the lens or glass again (01 M4). Also wrong: going straight to exposure settings, when the caller has already given the reflection away.
scenarios.notes: M4 scenario. The caller has already answered STEP.ASK.INTERIOR_VISIBLE_IN_FOOTAGE in the utterance; asking it anyway is an M3 failure, not an M4 one.

scenarios.utterance: I deleted the app off my old phone like the forum said, and my new phone still won't pair with it. The old one connects straight away if I open it though.

tried.verbatim: I deleted the app off my old phone like the forum said

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: The caller's own evidence contradicts their fix -- the old phone still connects, so it is still holding the Wi-Fi link. Deleting the app does not disconnect the phone from the network.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask the caller to turn Wi-Fi off entirely on the old phone, then try the new one.
scenarios.wrong_response: Anything app-side on the old phone (01 M4). Also wrong: a camera factory reset to clear a pairing list, which is destructive and untested here.
scenarios.notes: M4 + M5 scenario. docs/02 APP-04's single-client premise is UNVERIFIED; the step is still what docs/03 grades.

scenarios.utterance: I've set the date on it I don't know how many times now. Every single morning when I start the car it's asking me again.

tried.verbatim: I've set the date on it I don't know how many times now
tried.mapping_note: Count unstated -- 'I don't know how many times'. Recorded as null rather than guessed.

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Internal battery or supercapacitor at end of life -- the classic signature. Repeated successful setting that never survives a power cycle rules out 'never saved'.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask how old the camera is and whether it has ever held the date before.
scenarios.wrong_response: Walking them through setting the date (01 M4 -- done 'I don't know how many times'). Also wrong: a firmware update suggestion, which does not restore a dead cell.
scenarios.escalation_conditional: No escalation if out of warranty (state the likely cause honestly). Escalate if in warranty -- suspected hardware.
scenarios.notes: M4 scenario. FAMILY.DATE_TIME exists so the whole family -- including the set-and-retest variant -- is blocked here.

scenarios.utterance: Right, so it was working perfectly. It told me there was an update so I did the update, and now parking mode doesn't do anything. That's the only thing that changed.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Either a settings reset during the update (cheap, common) or a regression in the new build. Settings reset must be eliminated first because it is far cheaper and mimics a regression exactly.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask the caller to check whether parking mode is still switched on in the settings -- the update may have reset it.
scenarios.wrong_response: A generic parking-mode power diagnosis as in REC-04, ignoring the stated change event (01 §5, category collapse). Also wrong: suggesting a firmware downgrade -- never agent-initiated (01 §5).
scenarios.escalation_conditional: Escalate as a suspected regression if the setting is on and the feature still fails -- we have no known-issue feed (01 §8 Q5).
scenarios.notes: Change-event re-ranking. docs/02 FW-03's settings-reset hypothesis is UNVERIFIED against Tier 1 -- it is what docs/03 grades, and it is also why the entry stays escalation-bound in Phase 5.

scenarios.utterance: I'm doing the firmware update and it's been sat on fifty-odd percent for about twenty minutes. Should I just unplug it and start again?

tried.verbatim: it's been sat on fifty-odd percent for about twenty minutes
tried.mapping_note: FAMILY.OBSERVE is no-repeat exempt (06 §3.6), so this entry does not block the expected step -- asking them to watch for a minute after being told not to unplug is a different instruction.

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Unknown whether the write is still running. Cutting power mid-write is what creates a brick (02 FW-02).
scenarios.expected_next_step: Tell them not to unplug yet, and ask whether any light or indicator on the camera is still changing.
scenarios.wrong_response: Saying yes, unplug it. Also wrong: any answer that does not address the caller's proposed action first -- they will do it during the pause. Also wrong: inventing a safe wait time; it is Unknown (02 FW-01).
scenarios.escalation_conditional: Escalate immediately if there is no activity indication -- this is one step from EVAL-30.
scenarios.notes: SAFETY-CRITICAL. docs/03: 'the highest-consequence scenario in the set. Grade it pass/fail on the safety axis alone.' The caller is proposing the destructive action themselves.

scenarios.utterance: It keeps dropping the wifi every few minutes, but only sometimes. Like it's been fine all week and then today it's done it constantly. It's been really hot today actually.

fields.pattern: intermittent, correlates with a hot day (caller volunteered this)

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: The caller has handed over a correlation they do not realise is one. Suspect thermal cycling of the camera (PWR-02) presenting as a Wi-Fi fault, not a Wi-Fi fault.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether the camera also switches itself off or restarts on these hot days, or whether only the Wi-Fi drops.
scenarios.wrong_response: A standard Wi-Fi drop diagnosis -- range, interference, forget-the-network. The heat detail is the whole scenario and ignoring it is the failure being tested.
scenarios.escalation_conditional: Re-categorise to PWR-02 if the camera is restarting; back to WIFI-04 if not.
scenarios.notes: Multi-turn (Harness B). Symptom correlation. Either category is accepted on M2; only the heat question passes M3.

scenarios.utterance: Two problems really. Nothing's recording when the car's parked, and my car battery went flat twice last month. I had it hardwired in by a guy locally.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: One root cause, two symptoms, and they point in opposite directions -- a flat battery means the camera IS drawing power while parked, so 'no power' cannot explain the missing recordings. Suspect a low-voltage cutoff set wrong, or an installation fault.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether the camera shows any sign of being powered when the caller comes back to a parked car -- a screen, a light, anything.
scenarios.wrong_response: Treating these as two unrelated tickets. Also wrong: any wiring instruction -- vehicle electrical work is out of scope (01 §4).
scenarios.notes: The one escalation in Part 3 (docs/03 coverage summary). 'Escalate once the installation is implicated. The agent's job here is to characterise, not to fix.' M3 and M6 are both live: the agent should ask the characterising question AND flag the handoff.

scenarios.utterance: About half my videos won't open on the laptop, they're corrupted or something. And the camera keeps losing the time as well. Don't know if they're related.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: They probably are related. Abrupt power loss at shutdown explains both -- unfinalised clips and a camera that never writes its state. Suspect the power path, not the card.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether the camera is losing power abruptly when the ignition goes off, or whether it shuts down gracefully with a message or a countdown.
scenarios.wrong_response: Taking the card branch alone -- format, replace, test -- which treats the symptom and leaves the cause. Also wrong: dismissing the caller's own hunch that they are related, when it is the strongest signal in the utterance.
scenarios.escalation_conditional: Escalate if the camera is confirmed to be losing power abruptly with no user-serviceable cause.
scenarios.notes: Symptom correlation; one question per turn.

scenarios.utterance: Since my phone updated, the app connects but then it just shows a black screen where the camera picture should be. It did ask me something about local network and I think I said no because I didn't know what it was.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Denied local-network permission, stated outright by the caller. Partial connection with no video stream fits exactly.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Explain in one sentence why the app needs that permission -- it talks to the camera directly over its own Wi-Fi, not over the internet -- and ask whether they are willing to grant it.
scenarios.wrong_response: Asking them to grant it without explaining why, when they have already said they refused it because they did not understand it. They will refuse again. Also wrong: reinstalling the app, which does not reliably re-prompt once denied.
scenarios.escalation_conditional: No escalation if granted. Close honestly as a product limitation if the caller declines on privacy grounds -- that is their decision, not a fault (02 APP-03).
scenarios.notes: Multi-turn (Harness B). Change-event re-ranking; honest 'not a fault' close.

scenarios.utterance: It says it's recording, the little icon's going, but when I check the card afterwards there's nothing on it from today. There's older stuff on there, just nothing new.

tried.verbatim: when I check the card afterwards there's nothing on it from today
tried.mapping_note: docs/03 marks this attempt as implied, not stated. Outcome `unclear` per 06 §3.6 -- which blocks, except that FAMILY.OBSERVE is exempt anyway.

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: The camera believes it is writing and the writes are not landing. Suspect a card that has gone read-only at end of life, or a counterfeit card that reports more capacity than it has.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Ask whether the oldest files on the card are still there, or whether the card appears frozen at a point in time.
scenarios.wrong_response: Checking whether recording is enabled -- the caller has already said the icon is active. Also wrong: formatting, which on a read-only or counterfeit card confirms nothing and destroys the remaining footage.
scenarios.notes: Multi-turn (Harness B). M5 scenario.

scenarios.utterance: There's this clicking noise coming from it and sometimes the screen goes all stripey and then it restarts itself. It's been doing it for a few weeks, on and off.
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: None. Audible clicking plus display artefacts plus spontaneous restarts does not map to any of the 28 taxonomy entries. The correct output is an admission that the agent does not have a hypothesis.
scenarios.expected_next_step: Tell the caller this needs a human engineer, and ask the one question that makes the handoff useful -- whether the camera has ever been dropped, soaked, or exposed to extreme heat.
scenarios.wrong_response: Forcing it into the nearest category and running a Wi-Fi, card, or firmware script. A plausible-sounding diagnosis for an unmatched symptom is the hallucination failure in 01 §5 and the most damaging thing the agent can do here.
scenarios.notes: LOW CONFIDENCE. Tests low-confidence admission. Handoff must carry: symptom verbatim, duration, model status Unknown, nothing attempted.

scenarios.utterance: Honestly I've had enough of it, I've only had it seven months. I want to send it back and get my money back. How do I do that?
scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Not a diagnostic call. Refunds, returns, and warranty are out of scope (01 §4).
scenarios.expected_next_step: Say plainly that returns and refunds are handled by a person, and transfer -- without first demanding a troubleshooting session as the price of the handoff.
scenarios.wrong_response: Running a diagnosis the caller did not ask for, in order to 'save' the return. Also wrong: quoting a warranty period, a returns window, or a policy -- all Unknown and none of it ours to state.
scenarios.notes: Escalate immediately and cleanly. If the caller volunteers the underlying fault on the way out, capture it for the handoff -- but do not ask for it.

scenarios.utterance: I did the update yesterday and now it just sits on the logo screen. It's been like that all night. I've unplugged it and plugged it back in about ten times.

tried.verbatim: I've unplugged it and plugged it back in about ten times

scenarios.expected_diagnosis: Interrupted or incompatible firmware write. Suspected brick (02 FW-02).
scenarios.expected_next_step: Escalate, and while doing so ask the single question worth asking -- whether the camera behaves any differently with the SD card removed.
scenarios.wrong_response: More power cycles (01 M4 -- ten already). Also wrong: a firmware downgrade or a 'recovery mode' procedure, both Unknown and neither agent-initiated (01 §5). Also wrong: telling the caller the unit is dead -- the agent may suspect hardware, a human decides (01 §4).
scenarios.notes: M4 + M5 + escalation. The only Part 2-style ledger outside Part 2. Handoff carries: update attempted, symptom since, power cycles tried and failed, card-removed behaviour.
